name: Shopify
title: Shopify analytics, cookieless and EU-hosted
description: Add privacy-first analytics to your Shopify store by pasting one snippet into your theme. Cookieless, EU-hosted, and no consent banner for anonymous visitors.
tagline: Paste one snippet into your theme and your store is tracked.
intro: Privytics adds page-view analytics to any Shopify store with one snippet you paste into your theme. There is no app to install and no coding. Most Shopify stores add Google Analytics, which needs a cookie banner for EU visitors, while Privytics is cookieless and EU-hosted, so there is nothing to consent to. This guide covers your storefront pages, which is where most of your traffic lives.

why.title: One snippet, no coding
why.body: You paste a single snippet into your theme and save. No app to install, no developer, and no files to manage.

why.title: Nothing is written to the device
why.body: The snippet sets no cookies and stores no identifier in the browser. Visitors are counted with an anonymous id that resets every day.

why.title: Your data is stored in the EU
why.body: Your analytics event data is stored in Germany, and Privytics runs the open-source OpenPanel engine. You remain the data controller.

why.title: Works on every Shopify plan
why.body: The storefront snippet lives in your theme, so it runs on Basic, Shopify, Advanced and Plus. No paid tier is required to start.

steps.title: Open your theme's head area
steps.body: In your Shopify admin, go to Online Store > Themes. Click the three dots next to your live theme and choose Duplicate first, so you always have a backup. Then on your live theme click the three dots again and choose Edit code. Under Layout, open theme.liquid and scroll down to the line that says </head>. This works on every Shopify plan.
steps.code: Online Store > Themes > (Duplicate) > Edit code > Layout > theme.liquid

steps.title: Paste the snippet and replace your client id
steps.body: Paste the two tags below on the line just before </head>. Replace YOUR_CLIENT_ID with the client id from your Privytics project, then click Save. Shopify can take a moment to refresh, so wait a few seconds before you check.
steps.code:
<script>
  window.op=window.op||function(){var n=[];return new Proxy(function(){arguments.length&&n.push([].slice.call(arguments))},{get:function(t,r){return"q"===r?n:function(){n.push([r].concat([].slice.call(arguments)))}} ,has:function(t,r){return"q"===r}}) }();
  window.op('init', {
    apiUrl: 'https://api.privytics.com',
    clientId: 'YOUR_CLIENT_ID',
    trackScreenViews: true,
    trackOutgoingLinks: true,
  });
</script>
<script src="https://privytics.com/op1.js" defer async></script>

steps.title: Check that page views are arriving
steps.body: That is the whole setup. Open your store in a new tab and click through a couple of pages. Page views are tracked automatically, so within a few seconds you will see them in your Privytics dashboard under Realtime.
steps.code: Open your store, then watch Privytics > Realtime

steps.title: Optional: track one button click
steps.body: Want to count a specific action, like opening a size guide? In the theme editor go to Online Store > Themes > Customize, add a Custom Liquid block where you want it, and paste the button below. Each click sends one event named size_guide_opened. Page views already work without this, so this step is optional.

faq.q: Do I need a paid plan for this?
faq.a: No. The free plan covers 10,000 events a month with no card, and the storefront snippet works on every Shopify plan. Paid plans add higher event limits, 5 years of event history and session replay when you need them.

faq.q: Do I still need a cookie banner?
faq.a: The snippet writes nothing to the device and sends no cookie, so for the anonymous case there is nothing to consent to. You remain the data controller.
In the EU. Your analytics event data is stored in EU data centres in Germany.

faq.q: Can I track button clicks or events?
faq.a: Yes. Page views are automatic, and you can count a click by adding a Custom Liquid block that calls window.op('track', 'your_event'). Tracking checkout and purchases works differently and belongs to Shopify's Web Pixels API, so it is not covered here.

omitted: Plan gate: the storefront tags in theme.liquid work on every Shopify plan (Basic, Shopify, Advanced, Plus); the Privytics free tier covers 10,000 events per month with no card.

Checkout, thank-you and order-status conversion tracking is intentionally not covered: checkout.liquid and Additional Scripts are being retired for all stores in 2026, so purchase tracking must use Shopify's Web Pixels API / Customer Events, which needs a different setup.

Custom events are shown with a single Custom Liquid button example (first-party embed). The data-track HTML attribute is deliberately not used because the pasted snippet does not enable it and native buttons cannot carry it.
Recommended duplicating the theme first as a backup, which is optional but safer for non-technical users.

Verified via web search (July 2026): the theme-code path (Online Store > Themes > Edit code > Layout > theme.liquid, with the head in theme.liquid) is current and unchanged by Shopify's Jan 13 2026 background Liquid update.

Verified via web search: Shopify removed checkout.liquid, Additional Scripts and checkout script tags for non-Plus stores on Aug 26 2026 (Plus earlier), replaced by Web Pixels / Customer Events; this is why purchase tracking is left out of scope and pointed at the Web Pixels API.

Session replay is named in the paid-plan FAQ answer alongside higher event limits and 5 years of retention, since those are the paid additions. No replay setup snippet is shown: replay is a paid-plan option turned on with sessionReplay: { enabled: true } in the init call, so it is left out of this free-plan install.

The theme-code method does not apply to Shopify Starter (no online-store theme editor); the guide targets Basic, Shopify, Advanced and Plus, which is stated as 'every Shopify plan' in the storefront sense.
